column1: # Pikmin 4: Nintendo EPD / Eighting, Unreal Engine 4.26.2 (IoStore containers beside one pak, PhysX 3.4, MallocBinned3), SDK 10.4.8, NVN, Wwise sound, VP9 movies through the SDK's
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the Mac (docs/agents)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie: the title and the opening are VP9 movies)
# 30 fps, as on the Switch: the game steps a fixed frame time (bUseFixedFrameRate=True in DefaultEngine.ini, Unreal's default FixedFrameRate of 30) and asks for present interval 2
# (rhi.SyncInterval=2 in SwitchDeviceProfiles.ini, r.VSync=1), so a higher present rate would run the game faster, not smoother
# Unreal Engine 4.26.2: nninitStartup needs virtual address memory, sets a 6 MB heap for the C library's malloc and reserves one address region for the engine, 62 GB. This build reserves
# it only when -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= is absent (with the argument the region's base stayed 0 and the first commit failed into Unreal's fatal error), so no game_args:

# the rewriter's engine-wide gate on the store of its size (dm/tools/ue_region.py; hle_svc.c) gives it what the alias region has room for, 4.06 GB (until 2026-10-31 a cut of the default to 4064 MB in this build's patches.py). Its allocator, an FMallocBinned3 made on the first allocation (GCreateMalloc, main+0x353f770), cuts its pools out of that region; the constructor
# call is cut and the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone outside the guest block (the rewriter's engine-wide cut, dm/tools/ue_malloc.py; hle_uemalloc.c layout UE4_27), and the SDK's node

# area is cut to 62 MB with regions of 4 MB and more aligned to 2 MB, as SDK 20 (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py, the SDK-wide rules, the SDK 10.4.8 build). The region then holds what the engine maps itself: on the Mac, from the boot through the opening into
# the Olimar prologue, up to +1.5 GB of the alias region with 1.0 GB mapped, beside an Unreal heap of 1 GB and 1.7 GB of Metal allocations (about 2.8 GB resident). The region
# sits in Engage's 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region), as FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE's
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# A 3D game with a free camera on the right stick: the 3D pad layout. It plays with the controller, so it stays docked (1920x1080)
# The shader code archives of Carrot4-Switch.pak (ShaderArchive-*.ushaderbytecode, stored), each shader LZ4-compressed (uepak.py lz4_shaders): the engine's global shaders and the game's
# material shaders. Unreal combines vertex and pixel shaders per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs)
